articles.full_text:
THE glass door closes, and a curtain of cool air spills over your head, neck and shoulders, delivering instant relief from the punishing summer heat.
This is what it is like to chill in the Do Hiemon Box, an oversized stainless-steel refrigerator that looks big enough to fit a human being, because that is exactly what it is designed to do.
Trusco Nakayama has sold about 200 of the 1.5 million yen (RM38,483) booths to steel mills, construction sites, golf courses, universities and leisure facilities since it went on sale earlier in 2026.
As global temperatures climb, Japan’s summers have been getting hotter and more humid, with readings regularly exceeding 35° Celsius.
The country’s weather agency has had to come up with new terminology for sizzling hot days, while national broadcaster NHK routinely warns viewers of heatstroke risk.
During the season, pharmacies and household-goods stores fill their shelves with blue-toned products promising cooling relief.
Trusco’s contraption, effectively a tall box on wheels with a window and a bench that plugs into a standard electrical outlet, is meant to be used in places without easy access to air conditioning.
Following the recent earthquake that struck Kumamoto, the company sent units to evacuation shelters.
The Do Hiemon Box, which keeps the temperature at a brisk 15 deg C and blows jets of 5°C air once someone sits inside, is designed to offer quick relief from potential heat exhaustion or heatstroke, rather than serve as a lounge to sit back and relax.
Fumiaki Matsubara, general manager of Trusco’s product division, said: “The concept was less about providing a place to rest and more about providing equipment that could help prevent heat-related conditions from becoming more severe.”
Trusco, which has a market value of about US$1bil (RM4.1bil) and about 3,300 employees, mainly makes machinery and tools, as well as equipment for homes and offices.
The company has fielded inquiries about the human refrigerator from as far afield as Germany and the US, Matsubara said.
As extreme heat becomes more common, the company sees potential demand from shopping malls, summer festivals and other crowded venues.
Tighter government regulations to prevent heatstroke are adding momentum.
“Demand for our broader workplace cooling products has roughly doubled every year in recent years,” Matsubara said. —Bloomberg

DH reminds public to take precautions against heat-related illnesses during very hot weather
The Centre for Health Protection (CHP) of the Department of Health (DH) today (August 16) reminded members of the public to take appropriate precautions against heat-related illnesses, such as heat cramps, heat exhaustion and heat stroke, during very hot weather.
In a high-temperature environment, excessive sweating and difficulty in heat dissipation can cause stress to the body. Members of the public should take the following precautions:
- Hydrate in a timely manner to prevent dehydration;
- Wear light-coloured, loose-fitting and breathable clothing to minimise heat absorption and facilitate perspiration and heat dissipation;
- Keep indoor areas well ventilated and maintain appropriate temperature and humidity, e.g. by opening windows or using a fan or air-conditioning;
- Avoid strenuous exercise and prolonged activities such as hiking or trekking;
- Arrange outdoor activities in the morning or the late afternoon, if possible, and bring enough water; and
- Avoid beverages containing caffeine, such as coffee and tea, as well as alcoholic beverages, which may speed up water loss through the urinary system.
In addition, infants and children, the elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses such as heart disease or high blood pressure, overweight people and outdoor/manual workers are more susceptible to heat stroke. These groups should pay special attention to the following:
- Infants and young children: Avoid going outside when the temperature is high. If they must go outside, adults should ensure they stay in places with moderate temperatures and good ventilation or air-conditioning. Infants and young children should never be left unattended in a confined space such as a vehicle;
- The elderly, pregnant women, individuals with chronic illnesses and overweight people: Pay close attention to health conditions and seek help as soon as possible if experiencing any abnormalities in health indicators such as blood pressure, heart rate, etc or if there are fluctuations in health conditions. Avoid going out when the temperature is high. Make sure there is good ventilation, or turn on a fan or air-conditioner to keep an appropriate temperature indoors. High temperatures can also worsen the condition of people with chronic illnesses (such as cardiovascular and respiratory diseases). Therefore, they should have an ample supply of their usual medication and keep in contact with family members, neighbours and the community. People should seek immediate help if they feel unwell.
- Outdoor/manual workers: Reschedule work to cooler hours as far as feasible. If working in a hot environment is unavoidable, provide shade where practicable and use ventilation and heat dissipation equipment. Once work has begun, gradually adjust the pace of work and take breaks in the shade to regain strength.
The DH reminded the public that heat stroke is one of the most common health risks in hot weather. Over the past five years, there have been over 200 hospital admissions due to heat stroke each year in Hong Kong, with two to five fatal cases occurring mainly during the summer months from May to September. Vulnerable groups are more susceptible to heat stroke. Symptoms include dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion. In severe cases, patients may suffer from convulsions or become unconscious, which can be life-threatening if they are not cooled down and resuscitated in a timely manner.
Members of the public are also advised to pay attention to the latest weather, as well as the real-time and forecasted ultraviolet (UV) index released by the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO). When the UV index is high (6 or above), the public should note the following:
- Avoid direct sunlight exposure to the skin and the eyes;
- Apply broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen liberally, with a sun protection factor (SPF) of at least 30 or higher, when participating in outdoor activities. Reapply every two hours if staying outdoors for long periods, or after swimming, sweating or towelling off;
- While using DEET-containing insect repellents for personal protection against mosquito-borne diseases, apply sunscreen before insect repellent;
If symptoms develop, such as dizziness, headache, nausea, shortness of breath or confusion, rest and seek help immediately, and seek medical advice as soon as possible.
For more health information, the public may visit theCHP's heat strokepage andUV radiation page; the HKO's Dial-a-Weather (1878 200),latestweather report and forecast,UV Indexand weather information forhiking and mountaineering; andpress releasesof the Labour Departmenton precautions against heat stroke for outdoor workers and their employers when the Heat Stress at Work Warning is in force.

Environment and Ecology Bureau invites Xizang Autonomous Region delegation to Hong Kong to deepen co-operation in food, green development and trade
At the invitation of the Environment and Ecology Bureau (EEB), the Xizang Autonomous Region delegation arrived Hong Kong on August 12 to take part in a series of exchange and visit activities, including the Food Expo and the Chinese Mainland Premium Agricultural Products "Going Global" Exchange and Matchmaking Event held yesterday (August 14).
The delegation was led by the Vice Chairman of the People's Government of the Xizang Autonomous Region, Mr Zhao Peng, and comprised representatives from the Department of Commerce and the Foreign Affairs Office of the Xizang Autonomous Region, and Lhasa Customs. The delegation concluded its visit and departed from Hong Kong today (August 15).
The Xizang Autonomous Region delegation met with the Secretary for Environment and Ecology, Mr Tse Chin-wan, on August 12. The two sides exchanged views on the trade of agricultural products and food, as well as green development, and discussed ways to strengthen co-operation between the two places in the food industry, and areas of conservation and environmental protection.
On August 14, the EEB hosted a business luncheon for the delegation, which was attended by leaders from Hong Kong's four major chambers of commerce and trade associations, as well as hotels and catering organisations to jointly explore co-operation opportunities.
On the same day, the Xizang Autonomous Region delegation attended the Chinese Mainland Premium Agricultural Products "Going Global" Exchange and Matchmaking Event. At the event, the EEB and the Department of Commerce of the Xizang Autonomous Region signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen co-operation in the food sector, open up broader markets for quality agricultural products and food from Xizang, and promote the highquality development of the food industries in both places.
The EEB also arranged for the delegation to visit the Chinese Culinary Institute and the International Culinary Institute, and to meet with the Executive Director of the Vocational Training Council, Mr Donald Tong , laying a good foundation for future collaboration between the two sides.
During their stay in Hong Kong, the Xizang Autonomous Region delegation also met with the Financial Secretary, Mr Paul Chan; the Secretary for Culture, Sports and Tourism, Miss Rosanna Law; and the Acting Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development, Dr Bernard Chan. The delegation also visited the Hong Kong Palace Museum.
A spokesman for the EEB said that the visit marks a new chapter in the co-operation between Xizang and Hong Kong. Leveraging Hong Kong's unique strengths in food trade, green development, and other areas, the EEB will maintain close liaison with the authority of the Xizang Autonomous Region, with a view to jointly contributing to the nation's high-quality development and the building of a beautiful China.

articles.full_text:
An IMD yellow alert has been issued for the remaining districts of Uttarakhand, where heavy rain is likely at isolated places. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and intense to very intense spells of rain are also expected at isolated locations in these districts.
Orange alert districts in Uttarakhand
The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places in Dehradun, Champawat, Bageshwar, Udham Singh Nagar and Nainital.These areas may also witness thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and very intense to extremely intense spells of rain at isolated places.
Yellow alert for remaining districts
The remaining districts of Uttarakhand are under a yellow alert for isolated heavy rainfall. The IMD has also forecast thunderstorms with lightning and intense to very intense spells of rain at isolated locations across these districts.IMD warns of landslides, flash floods
The weather department has warned that heavy or intense rainfall could trigger landslides, rockfalls and mudslides at isolated places. Roads, highways and bridges could be blocked or washed away because of rockfalls, landslides and flooding.Heavy rain may also affect electricity and water services, while supply and transportation could be disrupted at isolated places for a few days. There could also be isolated incidents of damage to life and property.
Continuous heavy rainfall may increase discharge from dams and barrages, resulting in a rise in river levels. Major rivers and their tributaries could witness a moderate increase in water levels.
Heavy rain falling over melting snowpack may cause a sudden increase in water flow in rivulets and rainwater streams. This could lead to bank erosion, overflowing water and flash floods at isolated places.
Very intense or extremely intense rainfall could cause flash flooding and inundation in low-lying areas. In mountainous and steep terrain, rapid runoff could cause streams to rise quickly at isolated locations.
The IMD has also warned of possible damage to vulnerable structures, including kutcha houses, roads, walls, huts, under-construction buildings, bridges and tunnels. Railway operations, as well as district headquarters, government and private institutions, schools, hospitals, pilgrim sites and tourist destinations, may also be affected.
Lightning could result in isolated incidents of damage to life and property.
IMD advisory for residents and travellers
The IMD has advised people living in landslide-prone areas to remain alert. Pilgrims and tourists travelling to Chardham or other destinations have been advised to stay cautious and travel only when necessary. During continuous or heavy rain, travellers should watch for unstable or steep slopes.People living near major rivers, tributaries, rivulets, streams, low-lying areas and flood plains have also been advised to remain alert. Dam, barrage and hydroelectric power plant authorities should take necessary precautionary measures.
The IMD has advised that mountaineering expeditions may be halted, with expedition members moving to safe locations. Commuters and people travelling by vehicle should remain cautious and travel only when necessary.
People have been advised to stay indoors during heavy rain or flash floods and not attempt to cross active landslide areas. They should monitor weather updates through local media and other official updates.
The IMD has also advised people to avoid fragile hilly terrain and steep slopes, refrain from walking through flooded areas and avoid flooded roads while travelling in vehicles. Swimming or boating in swollen rivulets, streams, rivers and their tributaries should also be avoided during heavy rain.
State government authorities have been advised to take necessary precautionary measures to ensure the smooth movement of people.

Kheda, Matar record 1 inch rain each in 24 hours:Ahmedabad hottest as temperatures rise; heavy rain likely in South Gujarat today
Ahmedabad likely to receive showers today as well.
Rain was recorded in 103 talukas across Gujarat in the last 24 hours, with Kheda and Matar receiving the highest rainfall of 1 inch each.
Ahmedabad witnessed a change in weather on Saturday (15 Aug) evening, with showers reported across several parts of the city, including SG Highway, Gota, Chandlodia, Thaltej, Wadaj, Income Tax and Akhbarnagar.
Despite the rainfall, temperatures rose by 1°C to 2.5°C in most major cities. Ahmedabad once again recorded the highest temperature in the state.
Up to 9mm rain recorded in parts of Gujarat this morning
Between 6am and 8am today (16 Aug), scattered areas of Navsari, Valsad, Kutch and Junagadh districts received up to 9mm of rain.
The Meteorological Department has issued a yellow alert for parts of South Gujarat, forecasting heavy rainfall at isolated places.
Fishermen advised against venturing into sea
Considering the forecast of strong winds and rain along coastal areas today (16 Aug) and on August 17, the Meteorological Department has advised fishermen not to venture into the sea and to exercise caution.
Ahmedabad temperature rises 1.8°C as mercury climbs across Gujarat
Most major cities in Gujarat recorded a rise in temperatures yesterday (15 Aug), with the mercury climbing by up to 2.5°C.
Surat, which recorded the state's lowest temperature of 28.6°C on August 14, saw a rise of 2.1°C to reach 30.7°C yesterday (15 Aug).
Daman recorded the second-highest increase of 2°C, with temperatures rising from 29.6°C to 31.6°C.
Surendranagar recorded the sharpest rise of 2.5°C, with the temperature climbing from 31°C to 33.5°C. Ahmedabad saw a 1.8°C increase from 31.9°C to 33.7°C.
Rajkot recorded a rise of 1.5°C, from 31.3°C to 32.8°C, while Bhavnagar's temperature increased by 1.4°C, from 31.8°C to 33.2°C.
Dwarka records Gujarat's lowest maximum temperature at 30.2°C
Porbandar was Gujarat's hottest city on August 14 with a temperature of 32.6°C. However, yesterday (15 Aug) Ahmedabad recorded the highest maximum temperature in the state at 33.7°C.
Vadodara's temperature remained unchanged at 30.8°C, while Deesa recorded a marginal decline of 0.4°C, with the mercury falling from 30.7°C to 30.3°C.
Overall, Dwarka recorded the lowest maximum temperature yesterday (15 Aug) at 30.2°C. Most cities across the state witnessed a rise of 1°C to 2.5°C in temperatures.
Gujarat reservoirs fill further as six weather systems remain active
Widespread rainfall across Gujarat has led to a steady rise in water storage in dams and reservoirs across the state.
The Sardar Sarovar Dam, considered the lifeline of Gujarat, has reached 87.40% of its total capacity, with storage of around 2,91,970 mcft. The reservoir is currently receiving 39,163 cusecs of water, while 9,611 cusecs is being released into the river.
65.53% water stored in 206 major reservoirs
The state's other 206 major reservoirs have collectively reached 65.53% of their total storage capacity, holding around 3,65,566 mcft of water.
As water inflows continue to rise, 26 dams have reached 100% capacity and are overflowing. Another 41 dams have been placed under a high-alert warning, while four are under an alert signal and 12 under a warning signal.
Six weather systems keep rain activity active
According to the Meteorological Department, six weather systems are currently active over Gujarat, including a shear zone, Western Disturbance, depression, monsoon trough, cyclonic circulation and another trough system.
The combined influence of these systems has maintained a rainy weather pattern across the state. The department has issued a yellow alert and forecast heavy rainfall at isolated places today.
